About

Innovate at the peak.

Hillathon is an idea-only ideathon taking technology to the hills. Propose an original idea and a clear methodology for real challenges faced by hill communities. Design for limited connectivity, unreliable power, affordability and local needs. No prototype, code or demo is required.

Six challenge tracks

Choose your challenge.

Choose a track, explore its challenges and propose a feasible idea and methodology.

The challenge library

Find a problem worth solving.

Start with a track. Open a challenge to explore the problem, proposed approach and potential impact.

TRACK A

Water Technology

6 challenges
A1Low-cost IoT water quality monitoring for gravity-fed hill supply schemes

BackgroundMany hill settlements depend on springs and gravity-fed schemes with little routine quality testing.

ProblemDetect contamination events (turbidity spikes, pH or conductivity shifts) at source and storage tanks in near real time.

BeneficiariesVillage water committees, panchayats, households, schools.

GapsLab testing is infrequent and slow; commercial sensors are costly and need power and connectivity.

SolutionSolar-powered sensor node with local alerting and store-and-forward data upload.

TechnologiesEmbedded systems, low-power IoT (LoRa/GSM), edge anomaly detection, mobile app.

ImpactTime from contamination to alert; number of unsafe-water days avoided; cost per monitored point.

Departments involvedCSE (IoT, dashboard), ECE/EEE (sensing, power), Civil/Environmental Engineering, Chemistry/Environmental Science.

IP/CommercialLow-power sensing and anomaly-detection method; sold as a service to local bodies and NGOs.

A2Leak and pressure-anomaly detection in steep-gradient pipelines

BackgroundPipes on slopes face landslide stress, pressure variation and joint failures.

ProblemLocate leaks and unauthorised tapping without walking the entire line.

BeneficiariesWater utilities, village operators, downstream households.

GapsExisting leak detection assumes flat urban networks and abundant sensors.

SolutionSparse pressure/flow sensing with a model that localises faults using hydraulic simulation and ML.

TechnologiesIoT, time-series ML, hydraulic modelling, GIS.

ImpactReduction in water lost; leak localisation accuracy (distance error); repair response time.

Departments involvedCivil and Mechanical Engineering (hydraulics), AI & ML, DSCS, ECE/EEE.

IP/CommercialSparse-sensor localisation algorithm; software licence to utilities.

A3Rainwater harvesting design and monitoring tool for hill households and schools

BackgroundRainfall may be abundant yet seasonal, with water scarce in dry months.

ProblemHouseholds lack guidance on tank sizing, first-flush design and stored-water quality.

BeneficiariesHouseholds, schools, hostels, community buildings.

GapsGeneric design charts ignore roof type, slope, local rainfall and demand.

SolutionMobile tool that recommends system design from location and roof data, plus a low-cost tank level and quality monitor.

TechnologiesMobile app, rainfall data analytics, ultrasonic level sensors, GIS.

ImpactDays of water autonomy gained; share of rainfall captured; adoption rate.

Departments involvedCivil Engineering, CSE (app), ECE (sensors), Architecture/Design.

IP/CommercialAdvisory software and kit; partnerships with NGOs and local government schemes.

A4Affordable point-of-use purification with filter-life intelligence

BackgroundHouseholds in remote areas often cannot judge when a filter has stopped working.

ProblemPrevent use of exhausted filters and ensure treatment effectiveness.

BeneficiariesRural households, schools, health centres.

GapsFilter end-of-life is estimated by calendar, not actual use or water quality.

SolutionRetrofittable flow-and-quality sensor that estimates remaining filter life and warns the user.

TechnologiesEmbedded sensing, simple ML estimator, low-power display, optional app.

ImpactPercentage of filters replaced on time; reduction in unsafe consumption.

Departments involvedChemistry/Environmental Science, ECE/EEE, AI & ML, Mechanical Engineering (product design).

IP/CommercialModule design; consumable-replacement subscription model.

A5Spring discharge monitoring and short-term forecasting

BackgroundSprings are primary sources in many hills, but their discharge is rarely measured.

ProblemPredict dry-season shortfalls so communities can plan rationing and recharge works.

BeneficiariesSpring-dependent villages, local planners.

GapsLittle long-term discharge data; no simple forecasting tools for communities.

SolutionLow-cost flow logger plus a forecasting model using rainfall and discharge history.

TechnologiesIoT, time-series forecasting, satellite/rainfall data, GIS.

ImpactForecast error; lead time of shortage warnings; datasets created for new springs.

Departments involvedCivil Engineering/Geoinformatics (hydrology), DSCS, AI & ML, ECE.

IP/CommercialForecasting method; data services to agencies and researchers.

A6Rainfall-triggered early warning for water intakes and pipelines

BackgroundHeavy rain can damage intakes, pipelines and tanks through slope movement and debris.

ProblemWarn operators early and provide safe shut-off guidance for vulnerable assets.

BeneficiariesOperators, downstream households, local authorities.

GapsWarnings are regional and not translated into asset-level actions.

SolutionAsset-level risk map with rainfall thresholds and automated alerts via SMS/app.

TechnologiesGIS, rainfall data analytics, SMS gateway, simple slope-risk models.

ImpactLead time of alerts; assets protected; reduction in service outage duration.

Departments involvedCivil Engineering/Geoinformatics, CSE, DSCS, Environmental Science/Disaster Management.

IP/CommercialAsset-risk scoring method; licensing to utilities and disaster agencies.

TRACK B

Healthcare Technology

6 challenges
B1Offline-first telemedicine for low-bandwidth settings

BackgroundSpecialist consultations often require long travel through difficult terrain.

ProblemEnable consultations and follow-ups where video calls fail.

BeneficiariesPatients, village health workers, primary health centres.

GapsMost telemedicine tools assume stable broadband.

SolutionAsynchronous case-sharing app (text, images, vitals) with compression and store-and-forward sync.

TechnologiesMobile app, progressive web app, data compression, secure sync, optional voice.

ImpactConsultations completed; time to specialist response; travel trips avoided.

Departments involvedCSE, AI & ML (compression), Health sciences/Nursing, Biotechnology.

IP/CommercialSync and compression workflow; SaaS for health systems and NGOs.

B2AI decision support for preliminary screening by frontline workers

BackgroundFrontline workers must triage with limited tools and training support.

ProblemProvide guided, explainable screening prompts for common conditions and referral decisions.

BeneficiariesFrontline health workers, remote patients.

GapsExisting tools need constant internet and are rarely multilingual.

SolutionOn-device triage assistant with local-language guidance and referral recommendations.

TechnologiesEdge ML, rule-based clinical protocols, multilingual NLP, mobile.

ImpactAppropriate-referral rate; triage time; worker confidence (survey).

Departments involvedAI & ML, CSE, Health sciences, Languages/Linguistics.

IP/CommercialProtocol-plus-ML engine; licensing to health programmes (regulatory pathway to be studied).

B3Portable low-cost diagnostic and vitals kit with edge analytics

BackgroundBasic diagnostics are often unavailable near the community.

ProblemProvide a compact kit capturing key vitals with automated quality checks and flagging.

BeneficiariesRemote clinics, outreach camps, home-visit workers.

GapsDevices are costly, power-hungry or require trained operators.

SolutionBattery-efficient multi-sensor kit with guided use and offline analysis.

TechnologiesEmbedded systems, biosensors, signal processing, edge ML.

ImpactCost per screening; measurement agreement with reference devices; screenings per day.

Departments involvedECE/Biomedical Engineering, AI & ML, Health sciences, Mechanical Engineering (enclosure design).

IP/CommercialSensor-fusion design; device sale and service model (regulatory certification required before clinical use).

B4Emergency medical supply delivery in difficult terrain

BackgroundRoads can be cut off during rain; essential medicines and blood products may not arrive in time.

ProblemPlan reliable last-mile delivery routes and modes.

BeneficiariesRemote clinics, patients with emergencies and chronic needs.

GapsPoor visibility of stock and no dynamic routing for disrupted terrain.

SolutionInventory-visibility and routing platform with drone, porter or vehicle options, plus cold-chain monitoring.

TechnologiesDrones, optimisation algorithms, GIS, IoT temperature loggers.

ImpactDelivery time; stock-out incidents; cold-chain compliance.

Departments involvedCSE, DSCS (optimisation), Mechanical/Aerospace Engineering (drones), Health sciences, Management (logistics).

IP/CommercialRouting and stock-forecasting method; partnership with health departments (aviation regulations apply).

B5Maternal health risk monitoring and follow-up

BackgroundDistance and delayed referral can be critical during pregnancy and delivery.

ProblemSupport timely identification of risk signs and coordinate referral and transport.

BeneficiariesExpectant mothers, community health workers, clinics.

GapsFragmented records and missed follow-ups.

SolutionPregnancy tracking app with risk-flag rules, reminders, wearable vitals integration and referral alerts.

TechnologiesMobile app, wearables, rule-based and ML risk flags, SMS/IVR.

ImpactVisits completed on schedule; time to referral; follow-up coverage.

Departments involvedCSE, AI & ML, Health sciences (Nursing/Obstetrics), ECE (wearables), Social work.

IP/CommercialWorkflow and risk-flag engine; collaboration with health programmes.

B6Emergency dispatch and patient transport coordination

BackgroundAddresses are informal and ambulances face long, uncertain routes.

ProblemLocate patients and coordinate the nearest available transport.

BeneficiariesEmergency patients, families, ambulance and volunteer drivers.

GapsNo unified view of vehicles, road status and facility capacity.

SolutionDispatch app using landmark-based location, road-status crowdsourcing and facility readiness.

TechnologiesGIS, mobile app, routing, offline maps, crowdsourced data.

ImpactDispatch-to-arrival time; share of cases with accurate location at first call.

Departments involvedCSE, DSCS, Civil Engineering/Geoinformatics, Health sciences, Management.

IP/CommercialLandmark-location and routing method; contracts with health departments.

TRACK C

Food and Agriculture Technology

6 challenges
C1Low-cost soil health monitoring for terraced farms

BackgroundSlopes and terraces cause strong variation in moisture and fertility within small plots.

ProblemGive farmers affordable, plot-level soil guidance.

BeneficiariesSmallholder hill farmers, agri extension workers.

GapsSoil testing is infrequent, centralised and slow.

SolutionHandheld or in-field sensor with an advisory app for fertiliser and amendment decisions.

TechnologiesIoT, sensor calibration, ML advisory, mobile app in local languages.

ImpactInput cost savings; yield change; tests per farmer per season.

Departments involvedAgriculture/Soil Science, ECE, AI & ML, Chemistry.

IP/CommercialCalibration and advisory method; device plus subscription.

C2Offline crop disease and pest detection

BackgroundEarly disease detection is difficult without nearby experts.

ProblemIdentify common diseases and pests from leaf images without internet.

BeneficiariesFarmers, extension workers.

GapsMost apps need connectivity and are trained on non-local crops or conditions.

SolutionOn-device vision model with local-language treatment guidance and expert escalation.

TechnologiesComputer vision, TinyML/edge inference, mobile, dataset building.

ImpactDetection accuracy on field images; time to diagnosis; reduction in crop loss.

Departments involvedAI & ML, CSE, Agriculture/Plant Pathology, Biotechnology.

IP/CommercialDataset and model; licensing to agri-programmes and input suppliers.

C3Microclimate advisory for frost, hail and heavy-rain risks

BackgroundHill microclimates change over short distances, and generic forecasts miss them.

ProblemProvide farm-level alerts and crop-protection guidance.

BeneficiariesHorticulture and plantation farmers.

GapsForecasts are coarse and rarely tied to crop stage.

SolutionLow-cost weather station network combined with downscaled forecasts and stage-based advisories.

TechnologiesIoT, weather data analytics, ML downscaling, SMS/app.

ImpactAlert lead time; crop loss avoided; farmer reach.

Departments involvedDSCS, AI & ML, ECE, Agriculture/Horticulture, Environmental Science.

IP/CommercialDownscaling approach; agri-insurance and cooperative partnerships.

C4Post-harvest storage monitoring and spoilage prevention

BackgroundPerishables can spoil during storage and transport over long, rough routes.

ProblemMonitor conditions and predict spoilage risk in village-level storage.

BeneficiariesFarmers, aggregators, cooperatives.

GapsCold storage is scarce; simple monitoring is not common.

SolutionLow-power temperature/humidity/gas logger with spoilage prediction and alert guidance.

TechnologiesIoT, ML shelf-life models, solar power, mobile alerts.

ImpactPost-harvest loss reduction; shelf-life extension; income gained.

Departments involvedFood Technology, ECE, AI & ML, Agriculture.

IP/CommercialShelf-life prediction method; device-as-a-service for cooperatives.

C5Value-addition and processing planner for local produce

BackgroundSurplus local produce may fetch low prices at harvest peaks.

ProblemHelp groups decide which processed products are viable and how to produce them safely.

BeneficiariesFarmer groups, women’s self-help groups, micro-enterprises.

GapsNo simple tool linking produce, process, equipment, cost and market.

SolutionDecision-support tool and process-monitoring aid (drying, fermentation, packaging) with compliance checklists.

TechnologiesData analytics, mobile app, sensors for process control, recommendation systems.

ImpactShare of produce processed; margin per kg; micro-enterprises started.

Departments involvedFood Technology, Agriculture, Management, CSE/DSCS, Design.

IP/CommercialPlanner and process-control designs; branding and market linkages.

C6Market linkage and logistics aggregation for hill farmers

BackgroundSmall volumes and distant markets reduce farmer bargaining power.

ProblemAggregate produce, share transport and give price transparency while reducing waste.

BeneficiariesFarmers, cooperatives, buyers, transporters.

GapsFragmented supply, little price information, high transport cost per unit.

SolutionMobile/USSD-accessible marketplace with demand forecasting and shared-load routing.

TechnologiesMobile app, optimisation, demand forecasting, digital payments.

ImpactFarmer price realisation; transport cost per kg; unsold or wasted produce.

Departments involvedCSE, DSCS, Management/Commerce, Agriculture, Civil Engineering (transport).

IP/CommercialAggregation and routing algorithm; transaction-based revenue.

TRACK D

Energy Technology

6 challenges
D1Smart monitoring and control for community micro-hydro systems

BackgroundSmall streams can power settlements, but systems suffer from silt, flow variation and poor monitoring.

ProblemKeep micro-hydro plants running reliably with limited technical staff.

BeneficiariesRemote settlements, community operators, small enterprises.

GapsManual operation; no remote health monitoring or fault prediction.

SolutionController and monitor with load management, fault alerts and maintenance prediction.

TechnologiesEmbedded control, IoT, predictive maintenance ML, power electronics.

ImpactUptime; faults detected before failure; maintenance cost.

Departments involvedEEE, Mechanical Engineering (turbines), CSE/AI & ML, Civil Engineering.

IP/CommercialController firmware and prediction method; retrofit kits for operators.

D2Energy management for solar–hydro hybrid microgrids

BackgroundCombining sources improves reliability but needs intelligent dispatch.

ProblemBalance generation, storage and demand with limited forecasting data.

BeneficiariesHamlets, schools, health centres, small businesses.

GapsFixed rules waste energy and shorten battery life.

SolutionLightweight energy-management system using demand and generation forecasts to schedule loads and storage.

TechnologiesOptimisation, forecasting ML, embedded gateways, smart meters.

ImpactRenewable utilisation; hours of supply; battery cycles saved.

Departments involvedEEE, DSCS, AI & ML, CSE.

IP/CommercialScheduling algorithm; software licence to microgrid developers.

D3Affordable battery management and storage health tracking

BackgroundBatteries are a major cost and a common failure point in off-grid systems.

ProblemExtend battery life and warn before failure using low-cost electronics.

BeneficiariesOff-grid households, community systems, installers.

GapsCheap packs lack monitoring; users cannot see battery health.

SolutionLow-cost battery monitor estimating state of charge and health with alerts.

TechnologiesEmbedded systems, battery state estimation, ML, mobile app.

ImpactBattery lifetime gain; unplanned outages avoided; cost per kWh stored.

Departments involvedEEE/ECE, Chemistry/Materials Science, AI & ML, CSE.

IP/CommercialState-estimation method; module sold to installers.

D4Energy-efficient buildings and community facilities

BackgroundCold climates and inefficient buildings raise energy demand for heating and lighting.

ProblemIdentify low-cost retrofits and monitor their effect in schools, clinics and homes.

BeneficiariesHouseholds, schools, community halls.

GapsNo simple tool to estimate savings from local materials and passive design.

SolutionSensor-based thermal audit app that recommends retrofits and verifies savings.

TechnologiesIoT, building-physics models, data analytics, mobile app.

ImpactEnergy saved; indoor comfort improvement; payback period.

Departments involvedCivil Engineering/Architecture, Mechanical Engineering (thermal), DSCS, CSE.

IP/CommercialAudit and recommendation engine; services to institutions.

D5Clean cooking and heating with usage monitoring

BackgroundMany households rely on biomass, creating indoor air pollution and pressure on forests.

ProblemIncrease adoption and correct use of cleaner cooking solutions.

BeneficiariesHouseholds, especially women and children.

GapsImproved stoves are often unused or misused; adoption is unmeasured.

SolutionLow-cost stove-use and air-quality sensor with feedback and incentive tracking.

TechnologiesEmbedded sensing, IoT, analytics, mobile app.

ImpactShare of cooking on cleaner stoves; indoor PM reduction; fuel saved.

Departments involvedMechanical Engineering, ECE, Environmental/Public Health, Social sciences.

IP/CommercialSensing and feedback design; carbon-credit and programme partnerships (to be validated).

D6Outage prediction and fair load-shedding for weak grids

BackgroundWeather and terrain cause frequent interruptions in remote feeders.

ProblemPredict outages and prioritise supply to critical facilities.

BeneficiariesUtilities, clinics, schools, communities.

GapsLittle visibility into feeder faults; manual fault location.

SolutionAnalytics platform using smart-meter/IoT signals and weather data to predict faults and manage priority loads.

TechnologiesTime-series ML, IoT, GIS, edge gateways.

ImpactOutage duration; restoration time; critical-facility uptime.

Departments involvedEEE, AI & ML, DSCS, Geoinformatics.

IP/CommercialFault-prediction method; software to utilities.

TRACK E

Education Technology

6 challenges
E1Offline-first digital learning platform

BackgroundSchools in remote areas have unreliable connectivity and limited devices.

ProblemDeliver quality curriculum content, practice and progress tracking without constant internet.

BeneficiariesStudents, teachers, schools.

GapsMost platforms break offline or need heavy bandwidth.

SolutionLocal-server or device-based platform with periodic sync and teacher dashboards.

TechnologiesProgressive web apps, local servers (e.g., low-cost single-board computers), sync protocols, analytics.

ImpactActive learning hours; assessment improvement; teacher usage.

Departments involvedCSE, Education, ECE (low-cost hardware), Languages.

IP/CommercialSync and content-packaging architecture; licensing to education programmes.

E2On-device multilingual AI learning assistant

BackgroundStudents learn in regional languages and dialects with few digital resources.

ProblemProvide explanation, translation and practice in local languages without cloud dependence.

BeneficiariesStudents and teachers in multilingual classrooms.

GapsWeak local-language support and heavy models.

SolutionCompact speech and text assistant tuned to curriculum and local languages.

TechnologiesSmall language models, speech recognition/synthesis, quantisation, NLP.

ImpactComprehension scores; usage minutes; language coverage.

Departments involvedAI & ML, CSE, Linguistics/Languages, Education.

IP/CommercialFine-tuned models and datasets; careful attention to data licensing and safety.

E3Affordable virtual and remote laboratories

BackgroundMany schools lack lab equipment and trained staff.

ProblemProvide hands-on practical learning with minimal equipment.

BeneficiariesSecondary and higher-secondary students, polytechnic learners.

GapsExisting virtual labs need good internet and are not tied to local assessments.

SolutionOffline simulations and low-cost sensor kits aligned to syllabus experiments.

TechnologiesSimulation, AR/VR-lite, embedded kits, web apps.

ImpactExperiments completed; practical exam performance; cost per lab.

Departments involvedCSE, Physics/Chemistry/Biology, ECE, Education.

IP/CommercialContent and kit design; sales to schools and state programmes.

E4Teacher support and remote classroom enablement

BackgroundSmall schools often have too few teachers for every subject and grade.

ProblemSupport multi-grade teaching and enable remote expert sessions.

BeneficiariesTeachers, students in small schools.

GapsLesson planning tools and remote classes assume stable connectivity.

SolutionLesson-plan generator, recorded-lesson distribution and low-bandwidth live sessions.

TechnologiesLow-bitrate streaming, content distribution, generative AI with human review.

ImpactTeacher time saved; sessions delivered; learning gains.

Departments involvedCSE, AI & ML, Education, Media/Design.

IP/CommercialWorkflow and content pipeline; institutional subscriptions.

E5Skill development and local employment platform

BackgroundYoung people in hills often migrate for work, while local opportunities (tourism, crafts, agri-processing) lack skilled people.

ProblemConnect training to local livelihood demand.

BeneficiariesYouth, women, local enterprises.

GapsSkill programmes are disconnected from local demand and certification.

SolutionPlatform matching local skill demand with short offline courses, micro-credentials and enterprise-support tools.

TechnologiesRecommendation systems, mobile learning, data analytics, digital credentials.

ImpactLearners completing courses; placements or enterprises started; income change.

Departments involvedCSE, DSCS, Management, Education/Skill development, Social work.

IP/CommercialMatching method; partnerships with skilling agencies.

E6Learning analytics and assessment for low-connectivity schools

BackgroundTeachers rarely have timely evidence of learning gaps.

ProblemIdentify learning gaps and support remediation with minimal data entry.

BeneficiariesTeachers, school administrators, students.

GapsPaper-based assessment and delayed analysis.

SolutionCamera- or app-based assessment capture with offline analytics and remediation suggestions.

TechnologiesComputer vision (OCR), offline analytics, adaptive learning.

ImpactTime to identify gaps; improvement in targeted skills; teacher workload.

Departments involvedAI & ML (OCR), DSCS, Education, CSE.

IP/CommercialCapture-and-diagnose workflow; licensing to education bodies. Student data privacy must be a design requirement.

TRACK F

Economic and Livelihood Technology

6 challenges
F1Digital marketplace and provenance for hill artisan and local products

BackgroundHill artisans and small producers (crafts, handloom, spices, honey, tea, specialty foods) often sell through intermediaries at low margins.

ProblemGive producers direct market access and verifiable product origin without needing strong connectivity or digital skills.

BeneficiariesArtisans, self-help groups, producer collectives, cooperatives.

GapsExisting e-commerce platforms need good connectivity, charge high commissions and do not prove origin or authenticity.

SolutionVernacular, low-bandwidth catalogue and ordering app with QR-based provenance records and shared-logistics aggregation.

TechnologiesMobile app/USSD, provenance database, recommendation systems, image compression.

ImpactShare of price retained by producers; number of direct orders; repeat-buyer rate.

Departments involvedCSE, DSCS, Management/Commerce, Design (branding), Textile/Food Technology.

IP/CommercialProvenance-tracking workflow and brand platform; commission or subscription model.

F2Community-based tourism and homestay platform

BackgroundTourism can support hill livelihoods, but income is concentrated and seasonal, and visitor pressure strains local resources.

ProblemSpread tourism income to local homestays, guides and artisans while keeping visitor load within sustainable limits.

BeneficiariesHomestay owners, local guides, small vendors, local authorities.

GapsMainstream booking platforms favour large operators; there is little visibility of visitor load or local capacity.

SolutionLow-bandwidth booking and itinerary platform for local providers, with visitor-load forecasting and fair allocation of bookings.

TechnologiesMobile app, demand forecasting, GIS, recommendation systems, multilingual NLP.

ImpactShare of tourism spend reaching local providers; occupancy spread across seasons and locations; visitor-load peaks reduced.

Departments involvedCSE, DSCS, AI & ML, Management/Hospitality, Environmental Science, Design.

IP/CommercialAllocation and forecasting method; commission-based platform for local cooperatives.

F3Offline bookkeeping and financial inclusion for micro-enterprises and self-help groups

BackgroundMicro-enterprises and self-help groups often keep paper records, which limits access to credit and insurance.

ProblemHelp small enterprises keep reliable digital records and build a credible financial profile without constant internet.

BeneficiariesSelf-help groups, micro-entrepreneurs, women’s collectives, rural banks and microfinance institutions.

GapsAccounting apps are English-first and online-dependent; lenders lack trusted data on small hill enterprises.

SolutionVoice- and icon-based offline bookkeeping app that produces simple financial summaries and consent-based credit-readiness profiles.

TechnologiesMobile app, speech interface, offline-first sync, explainable ML scoring, privacy-preserving data handling.

ImpactEnterprises keeping digital records; loan applications supported; time to prepare a credit file.

Departments involvedCSE, AI & ML, DSCS, Management/Commerce, Economics, Languages.

IP/CommercialOffline voice-bookkeeping workflow and explainable scoring method; partnerships with lenders and federations of self-help groups.

F4Value chain and price discovery for forest produce and medicinal plants

BackgroundMany hill households earn from forest and wild produce (honey, herbs, fruits, medicinal plants), but quality, quantity and prices are poorly recorded.

ProblemMake collection, grading, storage and sale of such produce traceable and fairly priced while protecting the resource.

BeneficiariesForest-dependent households, collector groups, forest departments, small processors.

GapsNo shared records of harvest volumes, grades or prices; over-harvesting is hard to detect.

SolutionCollector-group app recording harvest, grade and price, with market price feeds and sustainable-harvest limits.

TechnologiesMobile app, GIS, data analytics, image-based grading, forecasting.

ImpactPrice realised per kg; share of produce graded; harvest kept within sustainable limits.

Departments involvedCSE, DSCS, AI & ML, Forestry/Botany, Agriculture, Management.

IP/CommercialGrading and sustainable-harvest advisory method; traceability service for buyers.

F5Dairy, livestock and apiculture micro-enterprise support

BackgroundDairy, small livestock and beekeeping are important livelihoods, but disease management, feed planning and collection logistics are weak.

ProblemHelp small keepers raise productivity and income through early disease flagging, feed planning and shared milk or honey collection.

BeneficiariesSmallholder dairy and livestock keepers, beekeepers, cooperatives.

GapsVeterinary access is limited; collection and quality testing are manual; no data-driven planning for small herds.

SolutionMobile advisory with image- and symptom-based early warning, feed and breeding planner, and collection-route scheduling.

TechnologiesMobile app, computer vision, rule-based advisory, route optimisation, optional IoT.

ImpactYield per animal or hive; losses from disease; collection cost per litre or kg.

Departments involvedAI & ML, CSE, DSCS, Veterinary/Animal Science, Agriculture, Management.

IP/CommercialEarly-warning and advisory engine; subscription service for cooperatives.

F6Remote digital work and service hubs for hill youth

BackgroundMany young people leave hill areas for jobs elsewhere because local opportunities are limited and connectivity is uneven.

ProblemCreate viable local income from digital and online services (data annotation, transcription, design, e-governance support) despite weak connectivity.

BeneficiariesYouth, women, returnees, local training institutions.

GapsRemote-work platforms assume reliable broadband and do not match tasks to local skills or support offline workflows.

SolutionOffline-first task platform with batch sync, skill-based task matching, quality checks and payment tracking at community hubs.

TechnologiesOffline-first apps, sync protocols, recommendation systems, ML quality scoring, digital payments.

ImpactLocal jobs or income generated; task completion quality; share of earners retained locally.

Departments involvedCSE, DSCS, AI & ML, Management, Languages, Social sciences.

IP/CommercialTask-matching and quality-assurance method; platform fee or hub-based service contracts.

Have a different idea? Propose your own challenge within these six tracks. View the submission guide ↗

Who can participate

Different skills. Shared purpose.

Teams of 3–6 Members

At least one member from CSE, AI & ML or DSCS. Interdisciplinary teams are encouraged.

Open to innovators

UG, PG and PhD students, faculty, researchers, innovators, entrepreneurs and registered or early-stage startups. School and community participants may join as problem-owners or co-designers.

Bring a guide

Each student team nominates a faculty guide; startups may nominate an advisor. Domain partners strengthen relevance and social impact.

Participation rules

One team per person. One idea per track per team. Women and members of hill communities are encouraged to participate.

Idea + methodology only

A clear idea is your entry.

01 / REGISTER

Introduce your team

Submit team details, your chosen track and a completed problem statement through the registration form.

02 / ROUND ONE

Up to 4 pages · PDF

Present your problem, proposed idea, methodology, technologies, expected impact and assumptions.

03 / IDEATHON DAY

7-minute pitch + 3-minute Q&A

Explain your idea and methodology using slides. No prototype, code or demo is required.

Your 13-field submission template
  1. Problem title
  2. Track and sub-theme (A–F), with cross-track links
  3. Background and context
  4. Specific problem to solve
  5. Target beneficiaries; mark unverified numbers as assumptions
  6. Existing gaps and limitations
  7. Proposed idea and methodology: approach, workflow, tools and data
  8. Technologies
  9. Measurable impact: metric, baseline and target
  10. Departments involved
  11. IP and commercialisation: novelty, prior art and who pays
  12. Validation plan: stakeholders and assumptions to test
  13. Risks and constraints: connectivity, power, cost, ethics and privacy
Evaluation framework

How your idea is judged.

Original thinking. Practical solutions. Meaningful impact for hill communities.

100pointsAcross 10 criteria
  1. 01

    Relevance to hill-region challenges

    Evidence that the problem is real and specific to hills.

    12points
  2. 02

    Innovation and originality

    A novel idea or significant improvement over existing options.

    12points
  3. 03

    Technical feasibility

    Sound architecture and realistic use of available technology.

    12points
  4. 04

    Affordability and accessibility

    Low cost and usability for low-literacy, low-bandwidth users.

    10points
  5. 05

    Environmental sustainability

    Responsible energy, materials and ecological footprint.

    8points
  6. 06

    Social impact

    Clear beneficiaries, inclusion and measurable benefit.

    12points
  7. 07

    Methodology and implementability

    Logical steps, realistic tools and data.

    10points
  8. 08

    IP potential

    Novelty and a defensible technical contribution.

    8points
  9. 09

    Market opportunity and startup potential

    Paying customers or a sustainable funding source.

    8points
  10. 10

    Scalability and long-term sustainability

    Repeatability, maintenance and local ownership.

    8points
How scoring works

Judges rate each criterion from 0 to 5.

  1. 0Absent
  2. 1Weak
  3. 2Adequate
  4. 3Good
  5. 4Strong
  6. 5Outstanding

Weighted score = (rating ÷ 5) × criterion weight

Fair judging & tie-breaks+

At least three judges assess each team. Judges declare conflicts of interest and score independently before discussion. Every team receives written feedback.

Tie-break order: Relevance to hill-region challenges → Social impact → Methodology and implementability.

Responsible innovation

Original. Inclusive. Accountable.

  • Submit original ideas and cite all sources, datasets and prior work.
  • Teams retain their IP unless a sponsor agreement states otherwise. Applicable institutional IP policies will be shared before registration.
  • Human field testing requires appropriate consent and institutional or ethics approval.
  • Use anonymised or synthetic personal, health and student data in examples.
  • Disclose generative-AI use; teams remain responsible for correctness.
  • Plagiarism, fabricated data and misrepresentation lead to disqualification.
  • The jury’s decision is final after review of formal grievances within the organiser-announced window.
The reward

From idea to lasting impact.

Shortlisted teams may progress to optional mentoring, validation, prototyping, IP guidance, incubation and pilot planning. The ideathon covers Identify → Ideate → Validate; Prototype → Protect → Incubate → Launch → Scale are optional follow-up stages over a suggested 6–18 months.

A message to students

Your project should be useful to real people. Before you build anything, call or message the people you want to help — a farmer, a village health worker, a teacher, a woman running a small business — and find out what they actually need.

Build something simple that works with little money, little internet and little training. Ask yourself one question: will this make someone's day easier, safer or better? If the answer is yes, you are on the right path.

The best idea is not the most complicated one. It is the one that people in the hills will really use.

From the field

Our work with the community.

A free medical camp in the Kunjapanai tribal zone, organised by our students and partners. This is the kind of work we want Hillathon ideas to grow into.
